baseline_findings.summary: Imperial cylinder constraints use max 1766 ft3 and retain metric min/step, rejecting defaults while permitting impossible gas volumes.
Travel manual depth limits disagree between markup, metric restore, and imperial mode.
Rounded display values become canonical physical inputs; Best Mix and CNS now reproduce the same unit-roundtrip drift.
Min-deco regression checks an adapter property rather than observable schedule behavior.
Cycle history allowed unresolved findings and a blocked prior record to be deleted or rewritten as passed.
Knowledge Base states that extending shallow stops is safe without qualifying oxygen exposure, gas reserve, or plan-recalculation limits.
Cycle 3 regressions compare rounded outputs and restore values before units, masking physical-depth drift and corrupting test state.
VPM-B+GFS copy says it helps when shallow stops feel too long, contradicting the app's accurate description that GFS adds a conservative surface ceiling.
Depth and cylinder edits after a unit switch leave canonical data-depth-m/data-volume-l stale, so consumers use old values and the next switch discards the edit.
Cycles 2-4 are marked reviewed although their protocol records fail closure and Cycle 4 has no evidence runs for five closed findings.
Cycle regression setup leaks canonical DOM and settings state, making the full engine suite order-dependent and leaving two contingency cases failing.
Browser trace evidence could pass forced or vacuous single-run checks without proving a real interactive consumer path.
Closure evidence was materialized from constants instead of executed commands, allowing fabricated exit codes, cleanliness claims, and unrelated trace reuse.
A dynamic deco cylinder created in imperial mode defaults to 0.4 ft3 while retaining min 1 and step 0.5, making its initial value invalid.
